Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third innings of the Test! The players are out in the middle. Oshada Fernando and Dimuth Karunaratne will open the batting for Sri Lanka. Nayeem Hasan will begin with the ball. Here we go...
... Third Innings ...

Quite difficult to see a result being forced out of this game! The wicket still is a decent one to bat one. However, if Bangladesh do manage to take a few wickets early, Sri Lanka then might just succumb under pressure. That will surely be Bangladesh's aim. Sri Lanka on the other hand will hope to bat and bat for long yet again. Their first aim will be to head into Day 5 with not much damage. Stay tuned for the reply.

Sri Lanka bowled well in bits and pieces. They will be very disappointed with the effort by their two spinners. Especially Ramesh Mendis who just never looked threatening. Lasith Embuldeniya did manage to keep it tight but wickets were expected from the two but both failed to deliver. The pacers though really impressed, especially, Kasun Rajitha who quite easily was the pick. The concussion substitute was brilliant and he ended with a four-fer. Fernando also did a decent job whenever he came one, he bowled with pace and ended with a three-fer.

Bangladesh's innings finally comes to an end! They end with a decent lead of 68 runs. This innings has really moved at a snail's pace. The over rate was slow and after the initial overs, the run rate also got slower. However, Bangladesh have batted themselves into a position from where it is difficult for them to lose the game. It is the experienced heads who stepped up for them. The likes of Tamim Iqbal, Litton Das, and Mushfiqur Rahim batted brilliantly. The three combined added over 300 runs for the hosts. Mahmudul Hasan Joy also played a handy innings. However, there were not many contributions from the rest. Had there been so and had Bangladesh played with a little more intent, they could have well had a lead of over 100.

Sri Lanka got off to a perfect start in this session. They picked up the important wicket of Litton Das on the very first delivery and followed up with the wicket of Tamim Iqbal in the next ball. Shakib Al Hasan came in and scored runs quickly but he perished soon after. It's the pacers that have done all the damage so far. The concussion substitute, Kasun Rajitha has been the leader of the pack. He has grabbed 4 wickets so far while Asitha Fernando has picked up two wickets. Mushfiqur Rahim and Nayeem Hasan were troubled a lot by the aggressive bowling from these pacers, but they have done well to survive till the break. Mushfiqur Rahim is still standing tall at the crease, he has notched up his century and will look to extend Bangladesh's lead in the final session. While Sri Lanka will want to wrap this innings up as quickly as possible. An intriguing session coming up. Do join us that 3:00 pm IST (9:30 am GMT) for the final session of Day 4.

Bangladesh are sailing on smooth water! The session began with Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das scoring runs freely and quickly in the initial first few overs. The Sri Lankan bowlers did put a lid on the run-flow but failed to trouble the batters. Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das are batting on 85 and 88 respectively and will be aiming to reach their milestones in the next session and help Bangladesh carry on the same way. Talking about milestones, Mushfiqur Rahim became the first player from Bangladesh to reach 5000 Test runs in the session as well. The pitch is not doing anything for the bowlers and as a result, Sri Lanka have been put on the back foot. They need wickets and they need them quickly. For now, it seems like Bangladesh are running away with the game. If they gear up, they can get a healthy lead by the end of the day and try to get Sri Lanka all out on Day 5. Well, there is still time for that. But let's see what we have in store in the middle session. Do join us at 12:40 pm IST (7:10 am GMT) for the second session.

Mahmudul Hasan Joy is down for a chat. He says that it feels great to bat with Tamim Iqbal, he has been the best opener for Bangladesh and it is good to open alongside him. Mentions that everyone has a dream to play for their country, he had a dream too and he likes challenges, and opening the batting was another challenge and he was well prepared to do so.

PITCH REPORT - The covers are off and the pitch is being rolled with a light roller. Roshan Abeysinghe is down near the pitch. There has been some rain in Chattogram since morning and the pitch has been covered. The good news is the sun is out for now. But there are still dark clouds hovering around. Let's hope the rain stays away and we get to witness a full day of Test cricket.

Bangladesh for now are in a commanding position. Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das have notched up their half-centuries and look comfortable at the crease. The duo will look to carry on the same way and will try to take the lead. Sri Lanka on the other hand had to toil hard all day and they managed to grab only three wickets. Kasun Rajitha who came in as a concussion substitute for Vishwa Fernando has been their best bowler. Surprisingly, the spinners have not yet taken a wicket. They will aim to grab a few quick wickets in the morning and take control of the game.

Hello and welcome back folks! We are now into Day 4 of this Test match between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. Till now we have witnessed solid batting from both sides. Bangladesh currently trails by 79 runs. If the pitch continues to assist the batters we could possibly expect a draw. Maybe it’s too soon to say that we still have two full days of cricket left and things could turn around.

Except for the second session, the Lankan bowlers were not at their best. To be honest, except for Kasun Rajitha, no other bowler looked threatening. The spinners did get a little purchase from the surface but the hosts' batters tackled them brilliantly. However, the Lankan bowlers just were disciplined enough. There was always a bad ball bowled in between which released all the pressure that was build built. Not only that, there were a few chances too which were not taken. Overall, the Lankans were not upto the mark on Day 3. They need to come out all guns blazing on Day 4. The visitors will need their bowlers to step up and deliver or they will end up in a position where winning the game for them will not be possible. The first session is an important one. The action begins at 0930 IST 1000 local. The build up though begins a lot earlier. Till then, goodbye and take care!

For Bangladesh, they lost three quickly but Rahim and Tamim have done well after that and ensured there were no more wickets to fall till Tea. The two are amidst a 36-run stand and Bangladesh will hope they can play for as long as possible. The hosts still trail by another 177 runs and the set batters need to cash in. The wicket is getting a little tricky as the game progresses so Bangladesh will know how important it is to get as close as possible to the Lankan total. Another important session awaits.

That is a really good session for Sri Lanka! They bowled with a lot more control and have been rewarded with three wickets. It was Rajitha, the concussion substitute for Fernando who was the star for the as he got two out of the three. Fernando was sharp in the short spells he bowled and he is the one who began things by get the opening wicket. The spinners bowled better lines and managed to keep it tight. Lanka could have easily had 4 had Tamim been caught off Mendis but they now need to continue to be disciplined and hit the right lines and lengths.

Bangladesh in response have started well with their blade. Their opening pair has stitched a stand of 76 runs and would hope their openers can make it big after a brisk start. Which team will hold the advantage at the end of the moving day? Stick together to find out.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of this first Test match between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The wicket has predominantly favoured the batters until now. Angelo Matthew's knock of 199 helped Sri Lanka to end with 397 runs. Although their bowlers have their task cut out, after a decent start with the ball on Day 2.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Bangladesh have begun well with the bat on a wicket which for now, is not providing a lot of assistance for the bowlers but there is still a long way to go. The hosts still trail by another 321 runs and they would hope the two, who have got their eye in can keep batting for as long as possible. Sri Lanka on the other hand will like their bowlers to be a little more disciplined and probably land more balls in the right areas which they did not do in this last session. Will there be more assistance for them on Day 3? We will find out. Do join us for all the action as Day 3 is set to begin at 9:30 am IST (4:00 am GMT). The build-up though will begin a lot earlier. Till then, goodbye!

Have to say, because of the last one, one and a half-hour or so, the day has belonged to Bangladesh. We entered Day 2, thinking Sri Lanka would probably be eyeing the 450-run mark. They began well too as they did not lose a wicket for most of the first session but once Chandimal got out, they lost wickets in heaps. Nayeem Hasan was the tormentor-in-chief. At one stage 350 looked far away but courtesy of Angelo Mathews who fell one short of a double ton, they got close to the 400-run mark. They did enjoy batting on this wicket and now it's their turn to toil hard on the field for some wickets.

Bangladesh have begun their reply in a strong fashion! They would have wanted to end Day 2 with minimal damage but they have finished it unscathed. Not only that, but they have also managed to score at a decent rate. Pretty sure they could not have asked for a better session than this one. Bangladesh had to put in all the hard work for 5 and a half sessions, but they eventually got Sri Lanka all out and ended the day on a positive note.
